summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG and stents, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for chest pain that occurred one hour after a dialysis session. The pain was described as squeezing with back radiation and diaphoresis, similar to prior myocardial infarctions, but was unresponsive to sublingual nitroglycerin. Evaluation showed stable troponin levels and EKG changes without diagnostic evolution, indicating angina rather than acute myocardial infarction. The patient was managed with increased isosorbide mononitrate (Imdur) to 120 mg daily, continued beta-blockade, and antiplatelet therapy. He remained chest pain-free, completed hemodialysis without complications, and was discharged home with cardiology follow-up and optimized anti-anginal regimen.
